The instant writ petition is not preferred against any particular order, but the same is being preferred against the inaction on the part of respondent No. 2 in not taking any decision on the application filed by the petitioner under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency of Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for Short Act, 2013).

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2 . Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is an owner of the land bearing Khasra No. 148, 149 and 151 ad-measuring area 0.19 hectare, 0.13 hectare and 0.84 hectare total 1.16 hectare situated at village- Shardapur, P.H. No. 12, R.I.C. & Tahsil- Wadrafnagar, District - Balrampur-Ramanujganj (C.G.).

He next submits that the aforesaid lands of the petitioner have been acquired for the construction of a dam in village Shardapur and after acquisition proceedings,
the award has been passed by respondent No. 3 and while assessing compensation the multiplier of Ramprasad Oyma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78934976/

sentences.text: 'two' as notified by the Government has not been applied and further no compensation has been assessed in respect of trees standing over the acquired land of petitioner and further no interest has been awarded for the period from taking over possession to the date of passing award as per provisions of Section 80 of Act, 2013 and thereby the petitioner has been deprived of getting proper compensation.

It is also submitted that on 06.07.2020 the petitioner filed an application under Section 64 of Act, 2013 before respondent No. 2 for the grant of proper compensation by applying multiplication of 'two', compensation towards trees and for an award of interest, but till date, the respondent No. 2 has not taken any decision on the application of the petitioner.
Thereafter, on 02.02.2023 the petitioner again filed a reminder application U/s 64 of Act, but no action has been taken by the respondent.
3. Learned State counsel submits that this petition may be disposed of with a direction to the respondent authorities to decide the representation/application of the petitioner according to law.

4. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
5.

Considering the limited prayer made by the petitioner, at this stage, to decide the representation,
respondent No. 2 i.e. Collector, Balrampur- Ramanujganj is directed to decide the representation/application of the petitioner within a period of 90 days in accordance with law from receipt of copy of this order.
6. With the aforesaid direction, this petition is disposed of.
